keptItems.title: Photos: The Student Protests in France
keptItems.summaryEvidence: Dimitar Dilkoff / AFP / Getty People gather on and around a statue in the center of Place de la République at the end of a demonstration on a day of nationwide protests organized by high-school students and joined by unions and teachers, who for days have been demanding better learning conditions, in Paris, on October 6, 2026. Stephane Mahe / Reuters French high-school and university students attend a demonstration on a nationwide day of protests and blockades, in Nantes on October 6, 2026. Demonstrators are voicing their anger over overcrowded classrooms, teacher shortages, underinvestment, dilapidated school buildings, recent police actions, and more. Olivier Chassignole / AFP / Getty Riot police watch a fire at a makeshift barricade set up by protesters during a demonstration organized by high-school students in Lyon on October 6, 2026. Philippe Lopez / AFP / Getty Riot police charge protesters at the end of a student demonstration in Bordeaux on October 6, 2026. Lou Benoist / AFP / Getty Riot police face protesting students who carry out a blockade outside Lycée Le Corbusier, in Aubervilliers, Paris, on October 1, 2026. Jean-Christophe Verhaegen / AFP / Getty A youth is detained by a riot police officer in Nancy on October 5, 2026. Tom Nicholson / Getty Students block the road outside Sciences Po during a protest on October 7, 2026, in Paris. Lou Benoist / AFP / Getty Protesting students gather and hold placards as they blockade part of Lycée Turgot in Paris on October 5, 2026. Yves Herman / Reuters Carole Zerbib, the principal of Lycée Vauquelin, talks with journalists

keptItems.title: Why American Cities Cost So Much and Deliver So Little
keptItems.summaryEvidence: Subscribe here: Apple Podcasts | Spotify | YouTube In this episode of The David Frum Show , The Atlantic ’s David Frum opens with his thoughts on the sudden recall of 12 B-1 bombers from their base in the south of England to the mainland of the United States. He asks what prompted the move and why the Trump administration refuses to learn vital military lessons from Ukraine. Then, David is joined by Reihan Salam, the president of the Manhattan Institute for Policy Research, to discuss why American cities cost so much and often deliver so little. They explore how some urban governments waste public money, how cities could provide better services to residents, and why the rise of populism is doing little to solve Americans’ actual problems. Finally, David ends the episode with a discussion of Every War Must End by Fred Charles Iklé. The following is a transcript of the episode: Reihan Salam: Well, David, I actually don’t believe that it is Donald Trump who is the only political figure who will have been discredited by this moment. When you’re looking at the Democratic coalition right now, I see a lot of anger and frustration with how people see their leadership class as well.
